objective: Installing and configuring storage devices: SATA and NVMe SSDs, HDDs, and RAID levels by use case
secondaryObjectives: Selecting a power supply by wattage and connector type, and choosing appropriate cooling for a build
Comparing laser, inkjet, thermal, and impact printer technologies and their routine maintenance

sources.cite: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1201) V15: domains Mobile devices 13%, Networking 23%, Hardware 25%, Virtualization and cloud computing 11%, Hardware and network troubleshooting 28%; launched 2025-03-25
sources.note: Exam page read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 ('Diagnosing issues: identifying and fixing hardware, network, and connectivity problems'). The objectives PDF (Exam Objectives Version 1.2) was read in primary text the same day: 5.5 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot network issues' lists 'Limited connectivity' and 'Intermittent internet connectivity'; 2.6 lists APIPA, static and dynamic addressing, subnet mask and gateway; 2.4 lists DHCP leases, reservations, scope and exclusions. The PDF says the troubleshooting methodology 'will not be tested' in the 220-1200 series but remains a competency standard. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's rogue-dhcp-soho-office (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The business, the users, the devices and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the IT technician for Larkspur Architects, a fictional 20-person firm. Three tickets wait this morning: the new file server's drives, a rendering workstation that shuts down under load, and a laser printer smearing toner.
handover: File server: four new 4 TB SATA HDDs, a hardware RAID controller, nightly backup to the cloud.
The rendering workstation got a second GPU last week; the power supply is 550 W.
howItWorks: The desk shows the ticket queue against the priority matrix and each service's status.
Move on a ticket round at a time. A decision comes to you at each ticket round; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.finding: The file server holds every project; it must survive a drive failure and stay usable. The workstation's two GPUs draw about 450 W at full load, plus 150 W for the CPU and the rest.

then.log: Round 2: one of the new drives fails early; the RAID 0 volume is lost and the firm restores from last night, losing a morning's drawings.
Round 3: during a render the adapter overheats and melts; the workstation is out for a week and the motherboard is damaged.
Round 4: you burn your hand on the fuser and the replacement is cracked when it is forced in; the printer is out for a week.

raidPrompt.title: Which RAID level?
raidPrompt.context: Four 4 TB drives. The firm needs to survive a drive failure, with as much space as possible for large project files.

choices.label: RAID 5 across the four drives (about 12 TB usable, survives one failed drive), keep the nightly cloud backup, and set up drive-failure alerts

effects.log: RAID 5 is built; alerts are on.

choices.feedback: RAID 5 gives fault tolerance for one drive with good capacity; RAID is not a backup, so the backup stays.

choices.label: Two RAID 1 mirrors (8 TB usable)
choices.feedback: Fault tolerant, but half the capacity, split across two volumes.

choices.label: RAID 0 across all four for the full 16 TB and speed
choices.feedback: RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy: one failed drive loses the whole volume.

psuPrompt.title: Shutdowns under load
psuPrompt.context: The system draws about 650 W at full load on a 550 W supply.

choices.label: Fit an 850 W 80 Plus Gold supply with the GPUs' PCIe power connectors, and check case airflow for the second GPU

effects.log: The new supply and airflow fix the shutdowns.

choices.feedback: Size the supply for peak draw plus headroom, with the connectors each card needs, and cool what you added.

choices.label: Remove the second GPU until a new supply is budgeted
choices.feedback: Stable again, but renders take twice as long.

choices.label: Use Molex-to-PCIe adapters to power the second GPU from the old supply
choices.feedback: Adapters don't add wattage; they overload a rail and are a fire risk.

fuserPrompt.title: Toner smears off the page
fuserPrompt.context: The printer is at 148,000 pages; the fuser is rated for 150,000.

choices.label: Power off and let it cool, install the maintenance kit (fuser and rollers), reset the page counter, and print a test page

effects.log: The maintenance kit is fitted; prints are clean.

choices.feedback: Smearing toner means it isn't fused; the fuser is due, and it is hot, so let it cool first.

choices.label: Replace the toner cartridge
choices.feedback: Toner isn't the fault here; the fuser is.

choices.label: Pull the fuser out straight away while the printer is running hot

effects.log: You reach in while it is hot.

choices.feedback: A fuser runs at about 200 degrees Celsius; handling it hot burns you and can damage the unit.

reflection.question: Write the work notes: why you chose the RAID level, the power supply and the printer fix.

parts.label: Storage and power
parts.criteria: RAID 5 survives one drive and keeps capacity; backup kept. 850 W for 650 W peak.
parts.modelAnswer: RAID 5 gives 12 TB and survives one drive; the backup stays because RAID is not a backup. The workstation peaks near 650 W, so it got an 850 W supply.

parts.label: Printer
parts.criteria: Smearing means the fuser; maintenance kit after cooling.
parts.modelAnswer: Toner smeared because the fuser was at end of life; we let it cool and fitted the maintenance kit.

expertPath.text: Read the specifications and the printer's maintenance log first.
Build RAID 5 with failure alerts and keep the backup.
Fit an 850 W supply with the right connectors and check cooling.
Let it cool, fit the maintenance kit, reset the counter, test.

raidHarm.headline: RAID by use case
raidHarm.body: A shared file server needs fault tolerance: RAID 5 or mirrors, plus a backup.

psuHarm.headline: Size the supply
psuHarm.body: Peak draw plus headroom, and the connectors each component needs.

fuserHarm.headline: Cool, then maintain
fuserHarm.body: Power off and let the fuser cool before replacing it.

target.headline: Good: right parts for the job
target.body: RAID by use case, power sized with headroom, and routine printer maintenance done safely.

partly.headline: Done, with gaps
partly.body: Nothing was harmed, but a decision was only partly right, or the record left something out. The criteria say which.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The record was not written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Choose a RAID level by use case: RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy, RAID 1 mirrors, RAID 5 survives one failed drive with more capacity, and none replaces a backup. Size a power supply for peak draw plus headroom with the connectors each component needs, and cool what you add. Toner that smears off a laser print is not being fused: the fuser is a maintenance item, replaced cool, by page count.
